title: Microsoft Teams: Facilitator on mobile takes notes of in-person conversations with speaker attribution
summary: Hold: the briefing incorrectly says its chosen availability route comes from the later Microsoft page; the Facilitator setup page was updated more recently. The control path and PowerShell command are documented, and the mobile-specific gaps were confirmed by targeted searches.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; rendered controls table; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Teams admin center > Teams apps > Built-in Teams agents > agent > Edit availability manages agent availability for everyone, selected users or groups, or no one.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Teams admin center and go to Teams apps > Built-in Teams agents. ... To change who can use an agent, select one or more agents and choose Edit availability. You can make an agent available to everyone, to specific users or groups, or to no one.

claims.where: controls[0].api; rendered controls table; Governance controls
claims.claim: Update-M365TeamsApp -Id <Facilitator-app-id> -AppAssignmentType Everyone is a documented MicrosoftTeams PowerShell availability operation.
claims.quote: Update-M365TeamsApp -Id 4c4ec2e8-4a2c-4bce-8d8f-00fc664a4e5b -AppAssignmentType Everyone ... Updates the availability value for Bookings app (App ID 4c4ec2e8-4a2c-4bce-8d8f-00fc664a4e5b) to Everyone.

claims.where: controls[1]: ui and api null; summary; Risk assessment: Change & support; rationale: risk
claims.claim: No tenant UI switch or automation specifically for mobile note-taking or mobile speaker attribution is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "Facilitator" "mobile" administrator switch PowerShell Graph speaker attribution note-taking. Read Facilitator setup, manage-apps, Teams Rooms and Update-M365TeamsApp on Learn; no mobile-specific tenant switch or API is documented.

claims.where: controls[0].note: first sentence; rendered controls table
claims.claim: The correctly documented Facilitator availability control is described with a caveat that Learn does not confirm mobile note-taking or speaker attribution coverage.
claims.quote: Built-in Teams agents like Channel Agent, Facilitator, and other built-in agents available across chats, channels, and meetings are managed from the Built-In Teams agents page, not the Manage apps page.
claims.fix: Replace the first sentence of controls[0].note, and its rendered copy, with: 'This setting controls who can use built-in Teams agents such as Facilitator.' Keep the separate caveat about automation for the Built-in Teams agents route.

claims.claim: Microsoft does not explicitly state that Update-M365TeamsApp also covers the dedicated Built-in Teams agents route.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams Built-in Teams agents Facilitator availability Update-M365TeamsApp PowerShell. Read manage-apps, app-centric-management, Facilitator setup and Update-M365TeamsApp; the cmdlet reference describes app availability but does not name the Built-in Teams agents route.

claims.claim: The Facilitator setup page documents allowing or blocking Facilitator through Teams apps > Manage apps.
claims.quote: In the left rail navigation, select Teams apps > Manage apps. ... Select Facilitator from the app list. ... In the actions menu, select Allow or Block.

claims.claim: The setup page says Facilitator itself is allowed by default.
claims.quote: Facilitator is allowed by default. However, if all apps are blocked for your organization, Facilitator is also blocked.

claims.claim: The setup page qualifies that default by saying Facilitator is blocked if all organisation apps are blocked.
claims.quote: However, if all apps are blocked for your organization, Facilitator is also blocked.

claims.claim: The app-centric management page links Update-M365TeamsApp for managing app availability through PowerShell.
claims.quote: For more information on PowerShell cmdlets for app availability, see Update-M365TeamsApp.

claims.claim: The two cited pages disagree about the route for managing Facilitator availability.
claims.quote: Built-in Teams agents like Channel Agent, Facilitator, and other built-in agents available across chats, channels, and meetings are managed from the Built-In Teams agents page, not the Manage apps page.

claims.where: Governance controls: 'the table uses the later one'
claims.claim: The agent and app management page used for the table is the later of the two conflicting Microsoft pages.
claims.quote: Facilitator setup metadata: ms.date="2026-11-04T00:00:00Z", updated_at="2026-11-18T06:40:00Z". Manage-apps metadata: ms.date="2026-07-05T00:00:00Z", updated_at="2026-08-18T22:08:00Z".
claims.fix: Replace 'The two pages disagree; the table uses the later one, and you should check which page your tenant shows.' with 'The two pages disagree; the table uses the Built-in Teams agents route documented on the agent and app management page, and you should check which page your tenant shows.'

claims.claim: Loop experiences in Teams control AI-generated notes for meetings.

claims.claim: The documented PowerShell setting for that meeting-notes control is IsCollabMeetingNotesFluidEnabled.
claims.quote: You can manage this control using the `IsCollabMeetingNotesFluidEnabled` setting in PowerShell.

claims.claim: That setting applies tenant-wide.
claims.quote: This setting applies to your entire tenant and can't be configured at the user level.

claims.claim: The meeting Loop control is not confirmed for phone-started notes.
claims.quote: Searched: Facilitator Teams mobile capture speaker attribution admin enable default transcription Loop IsCollabMeetingNotesFluidEnabled PowerShell. Read setup, Rooms and Loop admin-policy excerpts; none explicitly extends the meeting Loop requirement to phone-started notes.

claims.claim: The Teams Rooms page restricts identification and attribution to participants who add their names at the beginning of the session.
claims.quote: Currently, only participants who add their names at the beginning of the meeting session will be identified and attributed, provided that they have enrolled their profiles.

claims.claim: Those Teams Rooms participants must also have enrolled profiles to be identified and attributed.
claims.quote: Currently, only participants who add their names at the beginning of the meeting session will be identified and attributed, provided that they have enrolled their profiles.

claims.claim: Microsoft does not state whether the Teams Rooms attribution requirements apply to phones.
claims.quote: Searched: Facilitator Teams mobile speaker attribution identify speakers enrolled profiles notes storage permissions retention. Read Facilitator setup and Rooms; the named-participant and enrolled-profile requirements are given for meeting room participants, not mobile capture.
